newsitem.title: FRANCE: French beet planters see lower 96/97 sugar output.
newsitem.headline: French beet planters see lower 96/97 sugar output.

text.p: France may produce less sugar in the 1996/97 campaign than in the past season, mostly as a result of a decline in yields and area sown, planters said on Monday.

Assuming area of 422,000 hectares and a final beet sugar yield of "no more than 9.5 tonnes per hectare", planters are eying final output of 4.01 million tonnes, down from 4.2 million last year, an analyst for the French beet planters' association CGB told Reuters.
This was below the latest predictions by sugar intervention board FIRS and by the sugar manufacturers's association SNFS of national 1996/97 output of 4.05 million tonnes.
Data collected by the CGB up to October 20 showed some 50 percent of total beet area harvested and some 35 percent delivered to refineries.
Data also suggested that while sugar content was on the rise, beet yields were still lagging behind last year, the result of a dry spring that limited beet development.
Sugar content at delivery was 18.65 percent against 17.5 percent at the same time last year.
But beet yield stood at 53 tonnes per hectare, down from 54 tonnes on October 15 and 58 tonnes on October 20, 1995.
